title: I learned a lot of business through people's stories
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: This is a story, not a lesson. Read it and think about how you learn best.

groups.heading: I learned a lot of business through people's stories

lines.text: Jose said you have to get the book. Otherwise you will be kind of lost. If you don't read it, you are not going to get anything out of it.
It is one of the things I tell people all the time, he said. I learned a lot of business through people's stories, and learning from their mistakes, their good decisions and bad decisions.

I didn't go to business school, he said. But I have been in business all my life. I went and studied literature. I had to go through a learning curve on my own, and one of the ways I learned a lot was listening to people's stories.

groups.heading: A story about how somebody grew a business

lines.text: It is a lot more exciting, he said, than if I were to give you a financial management book from a university and we went into the technicalities of finance, versus telling a story about how somebody grew a business.

He said he prepares for class every single day to give valuable lessons. And you are definitely not going to be an entrepreneur if you are not at a speed of learning that is adequate to handle all this.
Whose story taught you the most?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the story that taught you the most about business or life.
Write what the person did, right or wrong.
Write what you will do differently because of it.

check.q: How did Jose say he learned a lot of business?
choices: Through people's stories and their mistakes and decisions

check.q: What did Jose say a story is, compared with a finance textbook?

recap: Learn from people's stories, their mistakes and their good decisions.
